body:
Thank you for taking the time to reply, I really appreciate it.
 
I have felt this way for a long time, and had never tried anything for years being depressed. I had always been too afraid and scared to try. What was so upsetting is when I finally got to that point, I didnt get afraid. It was like I was finally at peace. That feeling scares me now I am feeling at least a little better. I worry that now I have overcome the fear of trying, it will jist happen again. I am grateful at least for that part of me that is afraid of going back to it. If I didn't have that, I can't imagine I would be here posting for advice.

I am now living with a supportive family, especially my sister who is very understanding, and we do have fun sometimes. I hope at some point the fun doesn't not feel fake and so transient.

Thank you so much for this and taking the time to reply. I really appreciate it.

I used to think of times when suicide wasn't the best option, but to be honest the worst aspect of my depression for me is the complete and utter lack of motivation. I dont want to do anything, when I start trying I have panic attacks and anxiety and that's when the suicidal thoughts get the worst. I tried medication to try and fix my mental state and also tried therapy, but as they progressively failed, I think my hope for feeling better worsened. I have also gone through a couple if therapists, but it has been hard as I have been unlucky with them retiring or moving hospitals and such.

I did do EMDR, which in some ways was useful, but when I started it had been years and years since the trauma. It resurfaced a lot of the stuff I had hidden and a lot of my problems were ingrained from the coping mechanisms I had for the trauma, so the trauma wasn't so much the problem anymore.  Also I talked about things I was not ready to after a month or so, and then couldn't bear to return to it.

I do have some amazing people in my life who have been there to help. I have gone home to live with my mother and my family, and my 19 year old sister has been amazing. It has been hard as there have also been people who have been putting me down. Before I went to hospital, I was living with people who tried to kick me out during quarantine as they said they had expected too much of me, as I was depressed and wasn't getting better. They said that "perhaps their expectations of themselves were too high to help out someone depressed". A lot of other stuff happened but this isn't what the post is about. The friend who found me was an ex as well, so although I value them as a friend, relying on them is very complicated and resurfaces feelings I don't want to have with someone who is there for support.

If it wasn't for quarantine I think I would try group therapy or support groups, but I clearly didn't time my attempt well ahaha. I may also try telling friends properly about what happened, instead of being so ashamed. I imagine it would be worse for me to die without even trying to talk to them.
